move: Link the four uncrawled high-intent pages from the homepage in static HTML (new 'Go deeper' band in src/pages/index.astro), and correct the published test count 72 -> 98 in llms.txt, faq.json and rent-vs-buy-2026.md.

move: Fix seven published scenario links that used unowned params (price=/rate=/years= instead of pp=/mr=/th=), and add scenario-links.test.ts to guard the query-string contract across all published copy.
rationale: Scenario links are the intended distribution asset for phase D, so a broken one fails exactly where nobody is watching. Six of the seven looked correct because the values they named ARE the defaults. The seventh, in when-does-buying-beat-renting, told the reader to load a 4% rate to see a year-6 break-even but loaded 6.5% and showed none - the site contradicting itself on a page whose value is checkable math.
predicted_effect: No ranking effect expected and none should be attributed. This is a correctness precondition for D: pasted scenario links now load the scenario they claim. Success is the guard staying green and D's links resolving correctly.
outcome: 10 of 10 published scenario links now use owned params; guard added; 101 tests green, audit 13/13, deployed ad7bf2e5.

move: Build out the price-to-rent cluster: an engine-computed ratio-by-rate verdict matrix at /calculators/price-to-rent-ratio#chart, a new 'The math' guide (should-you-buy-in-an-expensive-city) arguing the high-ratio case, and both listed in llms.txt. Also guarded the previously unguarded threshold-ratio column and the guide's ratio-by-rate gap figures against the engine.
rationale: The only two ranking signals in 9 days of GSC data were 'price to rent ratio calculator' (pos 15) and 'price to rent ratio chart' (pos 41). The page ranked for 'chart' while carrying only a one-dimensional rate table, so the 2D matrix answers the literal query. The guide takes the high-ratio/when-renting-wins angle rather than redefining the ratio, to avoid cannibalising the calculator page for the same terms.
predicted_effect: Impressions on price-to-rent queries rise from their 2-query, 2-impression base, and /calculators/price-to-rent-ratio improves on 'price to rent ratio chart' from position 41. The new guide is a new URL on a crawl-constrained domain, so it may well not be indexed inside the window - that is an expected cost, not a failure of the content.
